title: Creamy banana porridge
summary: Smooth, slow-cooked oats with mashed banana and a little honey.
steps: Put the oats and milk in a small pan over a low heat.
Mash half the banana and stir it in.
Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until thick and very soft. Add a splash more milk if needed.
Top with the rest of the banana, sliced, plus the honey and cinnamon.
tip: Cook the oats well so they're soft. If oats bother you, use fine 'instant' oats or ready brek-style oats, which are smoother.
swaps: Use stewed pear instead of banana
Use oat or soya milk

storage.text: Best fresh. Leftovers keep in a covered bowl in the fridge for 1 day — loosen with milk and reheat until piping hot.

title: Soft scrambled eggs on toast
summary: Silky, buttery scrambled eggs on white sourdough.
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat.
Add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula until just set and creamy.
Toast the bread, spoon the eggs on top, then add pepper and chives if using.
tip: White sourdough is lower in fibre than wholemeal or seeded bread, and usually has a short ingredient list.
swaps: Serve on a soft white roll or crumpet

storage.text: Best eaten straight away. Scrambled eggs go rubbery when stored and reheated.

title: Banana & peanut butter smoothie
summary: A filling, protein-rich smoothie.
steps: Put everything in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Drink straight away.
tip: Use smooth nut butter only — crunchy has nut pieces. Look for jars that are just peanuts (and maybe salt).
swaps: Use smooth almond butter or tahini instead of peanut butter

storage.text: Best fresh. Can be kept in a sealed bottle in the fridge for up to 1 day — shake before drinking.

title: Yoghurt with stewed pear
summary: Peeled pears gently cooked with cinnamon, spooned over thick yoghurt.
steps: Peel and core the pears, then cut into small pieces.
Put in a pan with the water, honey and cinnamon.
Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until very soft. Mash lightly if you like.
Spoon over the yoghurt, warm or cold.
tip: Peeling and cooking fruit removes the tough skin and softens the fibre.
swaps: Use peeled apple, or add a strip of orange zest while stewing

storage.text: Stew a big batch of pears. Keep in a sealed tub in the fridge for 3 days, or freeze in portions for 3 months. Add the yoghurt when serving.

title: Fluffy banana pancakes
summary: Simple homemade pancakes sweetened with ripe banana.
ingredients: Maple syrup and sliced banana, to serve
steps: Mash the banana in a bowl, then whisk in the eggs and milk.
Stir in the flour until just combined.
Heat a little butter in a non-stick pan over a medium heat.
Add small ladles of batter and cook for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Serve with maple syrup and banana.
tip: Homemade pancakes avoid the additives found in many shop-bought ones.
swaps: Add ½ tsp cinnamon or vanilla
Use oat milk

storage.text: Cool, then stack with baking paper between. Fridge for 2 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat in a toaster or dry pan.

title: Mild shakshuka
summary: Eggs gently poached in a smooth, mildly spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
ingredients: 1 red pepper, peeled and finely chopped
steps: Peel the pepper with a vegetable peeler (or use jarred roasted peppers, which peel easily).
Fry the onion and pepper in the oil over a low heat for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the cumin and paprika for 1 minute, then the passata. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth with a stick blender.
Make 4 hollows and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook for 6–8 minutes until the whites are set.
Crumble over the feta and serve with bread.
tip: Passata has no tomato skins or seeds, unlike tinned chopped tomatoes. Sweet paprika keeps it mild.
swaps: Use crumbled firm tofu instead of eggs

storage.text: Batch-cook the sauce only: fridge for 2 days or freeze for 3 months. Cook fresh eggs in the reheated sauce.

title: Cheese & spinach omelette
summary: A soft, folded omelette with wilted, finely chopped spinach and cheddar.
steps: Wilt the spinach in the pan with a splash of water, then chop it very finely.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan, add the eggs and swirl.
When almost set, add the spinach and cheese to one half, fold over and cook for 1 more minute.
tip: Chopping cooked spinach finely breaks up the stringy leaves.

storage.text: Best eaten straight away.

title: Carrot & ginger soup
summary: Bright, silky carrot soup with a gentle warmth from fresh ginger.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized piece (3cm) fresh ginger, peeled and grated
2 tbsp crème fraîche or a splash of milk
Squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the carrots and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are very soft.
Blend until completely smooth, then stir in the crème fraîche.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and season with salt to taste.
tip: Blending makes soups an easy way to enjoy veg. Choose a stock with a short ingredient list, or make your own.
swaps: Use a little ground ginger if fresh is too strong

storage.text: Cool quickly, then fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Add the crème fraîche after reheating.

title: Butternut squash soup
summary: Velvety roasted squash soup — sweet, smooth and comforting.
ingredients: 1 butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and cubed
Squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Toss the squash and onion in the oil and roast for 25 minutes until soft.
Tip into a pan with the stock and nutmeg and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend until silky smooth. Stir in the cream if using.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and season with salt to taste.
tip: Make sure every squash seed is scooped out before roasting.
swaps: Use peeled carrot or sweet potato for half the squash

storage.text: Cool quickly, then fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Add any cream after reheating.

title: Red lentil & carrot soup
summary: A filling, protein-rich soup that blends to a smooth finish.
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, then add the lentils and stock.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils have fallen apart.
Blend smooth and add a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Red lentils are split and skinless, so they're much gentler than whole beans. Start with small portions if pulses are new to you.
swaps: Add a peeled sweet potato for a sweeter soup

storage.text: Thickens as it stands. Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months; loosen with water when reheating.

title: Tomato soup & grilled cheese
summary: Smooth homemade tomato soup with a golden cheese toastie for dipping.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 8 minutes.
Add the passata, stock and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend smooth and stir in the cream.
Butter the outside of the bread, fill with cheese and cook in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes each side until golden.
tip: Homemade soup avoids the thickeners and additives in many tinned soups.

storage.text: Batch-cook the soup: fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Make the toastie fresh.

title: Potato & leek soup
summary: A classic creamy soup, blended until totally smooth.
steps: Melt the butter and cook the leeks gently for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the potatoes, stock and bay leaf and simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, add the milk and blend until completely smooth. Season to taste.
tip: Use only the pale part of the leek — the dark green tops are tougher and more fibrous.

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Potato soup can go a little grainy when frozen — blend again after reheating.

title: Hummus & roast pepper wrap
summary: Soft tortilla with smooth hummus, peeled roast peppers and feta.
ingredients: 3 tbsp smooth hummus (see the homemade hummus recipe)
2 jarred roasted red peppers, skins removed
steps: Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for a few seconds.
Spread with hummus.
Slice the peppers into strips, checking for any skin, and lay them on top.
Crumble over the feta, roll up tightly and cut in half.
tip: Jarred peppers are already cooked and peel easily — check every strip for skin.

storage.text: Best made fresh. Can be wrapped and kept in the fridge until the next day.

title: Egg mayo sandwich
summary: Hard-boiled eggs mashed with mayo and chives on soft white bread.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Mash with the mayo, yoghurt, chives, salt and pepper.
Spread between the bread and cut into halves.
tip: Pick a mayonnaise with a short ingredient list, or mix half-and-half with yoghurt.

storage.text: Keep the egg mayo filling in a sealed tub in the fridge for 2 days. Make sandwiches fresh. Don't freeze.

title: Courgette & feta fritters
summary: Golden fritters made with peeled, grated courgette and salty feta.
ingredients: 2 tbsp finely chopped mint or dill
steps: Grate the peeled courgettes, then squeeze out as much water as you can in a clean tea towel.
Mix with the feta, eggs, flour and herbs.
Heat oil in a frying pan and add spoonfuls of the mix, flattening slightly.
Cook for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through. Serve with yoghurt.
tip: Peeling courgettes removes the tougher skin; the soft flesh is usually well tolerated when cooked.

storage.text: Cool, then fridge for 2 days or freeze between baking paper for 2 months. Reheat in the oven until hot all the way through.

title: Avocado & egg on toast
summary: Smashed avocado with a squeeze of lemon and a soft poached egg.
steps: Mash the avocado with the lemon, salt and pepper until smooth.
Poach the eggs in gently simmering water for 3 minutes.
Toast the bread, spread with avocado and top with the eggs.
tip: Skip chilli flakes and seeds that are often added to this dish.

storage.text: Best eaten straight away — avocado browns quickly.

title: Butternut squash dhal
summary: Mild, creamy red lentil dhal with soft squash and coconut milk.
ingredients: 300g butternut squash, peeled and diced small
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, squash, coconut milk and stock.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the squash breaks up.
Mash or blend some of it for a smoother texture. Serve with rice.
tip: No chilli — the flavour comes from warming spices instead. White rice is lower in fibre than brown.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato instead of squash

storage.text: Great for batch cooking. Fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day; reheat only once.

title: Butternut squash risotto
summary: Creamy risotto with soft roasted squash and parmesan-style cheese.
steps: Roast the squash in the oil at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes. Mash half of it.
Meanwhile, melt the butter and soften the onion for 5 minutes, adding the sage, finely chopped.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 20 minutes.
Stir in the mashed squash, the cubes and the cheese. Rest for 2 minutes before serving.
tip: Traditional parmesan isn't vegetarian — look for a vegetarian hard cheese. Risotto rice is soft and low in fibre.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato instead of squash

storage.text: Risotto contains rice, so cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Reheat only once, until steaming hot. Don't freeze.

title: Lemon & spinach risotto
summary: Fresh, bright risotto with wilted spinach blended into the rice.
ingredients: 1 lemon, zested and juiced (add juice to taste)
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18–20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wilt the spinach and blend it with a splash of stock to a smooth purée.
Stir the spinach purée, lemon, cheese and mascarpone into the rice.
tip: Blending the spinach gives you the greens without the stringy leaves.

storage.text: Risotto contains rice, so cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Reheat only once, until steaming hot. Don't freeze.

title: Butternut mac & cheese
summary: Homemade cheese sauce with puréed squash hidden inside.
steps: Boil the squash for 12 minutes until soft, then mash or blend smooth.
Cook the macaroni until soft. Drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk until thick.
Stir in the squash, most of the cheese, the mustard and nutmeg.
Mix with the pasta, top with the rest of the cheese and grill until bubbling.
tip: Cook pasta a little past al dente on harder days — softer pasta is easier to digest.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato instead of squash

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days or freeze in portions for 2 months. Add a splash of milk when reheating.

title: Sticky honey-soy tofu with rice
summary: Crispy tofu in a sticky, garlicky glaze with soft carrots and rice.
ingredients: 280g calcium-set firm tofu, pressed and cubed
steps: Toss the tofu in the cornflour.
Fry in the oil for 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden.
Steam or boil the carrots for 8 minutes until very soft.
Mix the soy, honey, vinegar, garlic and ginger, pour into the pan and bubble until sticky. Toss the carrots through.
Serve over rice with the carrots.
tip: Leave off the sesame seeds that usually top this dish. Plain tofu is a minimally processed protein.
swaps: Use maple syrup to make it vegan

storage.text: Store the tofu and carrots for 2 days in the fridge. Cooked rice must be cooled within 1 hour and eaten within 1 day.

title: Mild butter paneer
summary: Paneer in a smooth, creamy tomato sauce — all flavour, no heat.
ingredients: White basmati rice or plain naan, to serve
steps: Fry the paneer in half the butter until golden. Set aside.
Melt the rest of the butter and soften the onion for 8 minutes. Add garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the passata and simmer for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Stir in the cream, honey and paneer and heat through.
tip: Leave out chilli and fresh green chillies. Blending the sauce removes onion pieces.
swaps: Use firm tofu instead of paneer
Use coconut milk instead of cream

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. The sauce freezes well; add a splash of cream when reheating. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day; reheat only once.

servedWith: White basmati rice or plain naan

title: Gnocchi & mozzarella bake
summary: Soft potato gnocchi baked in tomato sauce with melting mozzarella.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Warm the oil and garlic, add the passata and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir the raw gnocchi straight into the sauce — no need to boil them first.
Tip into a baking dish, top with mozzarella and bake for 20 minutes, covered for the first 10, until bubbling. Scatter over basil.
tip: Choose gnocchi with a short ingredient list (mostly potato and flour), or make your own.
swaps: Use cheddar instead of mozzarella

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Gnocchi goes soft when frozen, but you can freeze the sauce on its own for 3 months.

title: Lentil shepherd's pie
summary: Rich red lentil and carrot filling under fluffy, buttery mash.
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetarian Worcestershire sauce or soy sauce
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the lentils, tomato purée, Worcestershire, stock and thyme. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until soft and mash with the butter and milk.
Spoon the filling into a dish, top with mash and cheese.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes until golden.
tip: No peas here — their skins can be hard to break down. Standard Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies — use a vegetarian one or soy.
swaps: Top with mashed sweet potato instead

storage.text: Ideal for batch cooking. Fridge for 3 days or freeze (whole or in portions) for 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight, then reheat until piping hot.

title: Cauliflower cheese
summary: Tender cauliflower in a golden, bubbling cheddar sauce.
ingredients: 1 cauliflower, cut into small florets (stalks removed)
steps: Boil the florets for 8–10 minutes until very tender. Drain well.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then slowly whisk in the milk until thick.
Stir in most of the cheese and the mustard and nutmeg.
Pour over the cauliflower, top with the rest of the cheese and grill until golden.
tip: Use only the florets and cook them until very soft. Cauliflower can cause wind for some people, so try a small portion first.

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat in the oven until bubbling.

title: Halloumi & peeled veg traybake
summary: Roasted sweet potato, carrots and courgette with golden halloumi.
ingredients: 3 carrots, peeled and cut into 1cm slices
1 courgette, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Toss the veg with oil and oregano on a large tray. Cover with foil for the first 20 minutes so it steams soft, then uncover and roast for 10 more minutes.
Add the halloumi slices and roast for 10–15 minutes more until golden.
Finish with lemon.
tip: Roast until the veg is soft all the way through, not crunchy at the edges.
swaps: Use firm tofu or paneer instead of halloumi

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Halloumi goes rubbery if frozen, but the roast veg alone freezes for 2 months.

title: Simple egg fried rice
summary: Quick fried rice with egg and soft carrot — no peas or sweetcorn.
ingredients: 1 spring onion, green part only, finely sliced
steps: Heat the oil in a wok and cook the grated carrot for 2–3 minutes until soft.
Push to one side, add the eggs and scramble.
Add the rice and soy sauce and stir-fry until piping hot.
Stir in the spring onion for the last minute so it softens.
tip: Shop and takeaway versions usually include peas and sweetcorn — making it yourself avoids both.
swaps: Add cubes of firm tofu for extra protein

storage.text: Cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Reheat only once, until steaming hot. Don't freeze.

title: Creamy roast pepper pasta
summary: Pasta in a silky blended sauce of roast peppers and cream cheese.
steps: Cook the pasta. Keep a cup of the water.
Soften the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, then blend with the peppers, cream cheese and hard cheese until very smooth.
Warm the sauce in the pan, loosening with pasta water.
Toss with the pasta and top with basil.
tip: Blending the peppers removes any bits of skin.
swaps: Use ricotta instead of cream cheese

storage.text: Sauce: fridge for 2 days or freeze for 3 months. Cooked pasta with sauce keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Spinach & ricotta pasta bake
summary: Pasta shells baked with tomato sauce, creamy ricotta and blended spinach.
steps: Cook the pasta until soft. Drain.
Wilt the spinach, squeeze dry and blend or chop very finely. Mix with the ricotta, egg and nutmeg.
Warm the passata with the garlic for 5 minutes.
Mix the pasta with the sauce, dollop over the ricotta mix and top with mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes.
tip: Finely chopped or blended spinach is easier to digest than whole leaves.
swaps: Use blended cottage cheese instead of ricotta

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat covered in the oven until hot all the way through.

title: Miso noodle soup with tofu
summary: A light, soothing broth with soft noodles and silken tofu.
ingredients: 300g straight-to-wok udon or 150g dried rice noodles
1 carrot, peeled and cut into thin ribbons
steps: Bring the water to a simmer with the ginger and carrot. Cook for 8–10 minutes until the carrot is very soft.
Add the noodles and cook as the packet says.
Turn off the heat, then whisk in the miso and soy.
Add the tofu gently and serve.
tip: Don't boil the miso — add it off the heat. Udon noodles are soft and low in fibre.

storage.text: Best fresh. The broth (without noodles or tofu) keeps 1 day in the fridge.

title: Mild sweet potato & coconut curry
summary: A gentle, creamy curry with peeled sweet potato and spinach.
ingredients: Squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, coconut milk and stock. Simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then blend the spinach with a ladle of the sauce until smooth and stir back in.
Serve with rice.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and season with salt to taste.
tip: Pick a 'mild' curry powder and check it has no chilli listed high up.
swaps: Use butternut squash instead of sweet potato

storage.text: Great for batch cooking. Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Cook rice fresh. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day; reheat only once.

title: Creamy baked eggs
summary: Eggs baked in little dishes with cream, spinach purée and cheese.
ingredients: 50g spinach, wilted and blended to a purée
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter 2 ramekins.
Divide the spinach between them, crack 2 eggs into each and spoon over the cream.
Top with cheese and bake for 12–15 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve with toast for dipping.
tip: A quick, soft, high-protein meal for days when you don't feel like much.

storage.text: Best eaten straight away.

title: Cheesy polenta with tomato sauce
summary: Soft, creamy polenta topped with a slow-simmered smooth tomato sauce.
steps: Warm the oil and garlic, add the passata and simmer for 15 minutes.
Bring the stock to the boil and whisk in the polenta. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until thick.
Beat in the butter and cheese.
Spoon into bowls and top with the sauce and basil.
tip: Polenta is made from finely ground corn, without the tough husks of whole sweetcorn kernels. Try a small portion first.

storage.text: Polenta sets firm in the fridge (2 days) — slice and fry it, or reheat with milk. The tomato sauce freezes for 3 months.

title: Stewed apple & custard
summary: Soft cinnamon apple with simple homemade custard.
steps: Simmer the apples, sugar, cinnamon and water with a lid on for 10 minutes until soft.
For the custard, heat the milk until steaming.
Whisk the yolks, sugar, cornflour and vanilla, then slowly whisk in the hot milk.
Return to the pan and stir over a low heat until thick. Pour over the apples.
tip: Homemade custard avoids colourings and thickeners in many ready-made versions.

storage.text: Stewed apple keeps 3 days in the fridge or freezes for 3 months. Custard keeps 2 days in the fridge — don't freeze it.

title: Creamy rice pudding
summary: Slow-cooked pudding rice in vanilla milk — pure comfort.
steps: Put the rice, milk, sugar and vanilla in a pan.
Simmer very gently for 40–45 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the butter and top with nutmeg.
tip: Very soft and filling — handy on harder days.
swaps: Use oat or soya milk and maple syrup to make it vegan

storage.text: Cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Eat cold, or reheat once until steaming hot. Don't freeze.

title: Simple banana bread
summary: Moist, nut-free banana bread with a short, simple ingredient list.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a loaf tin.
Mash the bananas, then stir in the butter, sugar, egg and vanilla.
Fold in the bicarb, salt and flour.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50–60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
tip: No walnuts or seeds — just plain banana bread.
swaps: Use oil instead of butter

storage.text: Keep wrapped in a tin at room temperature for 3 days. Freeze whole or in slices for 3 months.

title: Silky homemade hummus
summary: Extra-smooth hummus with warm pitta for dipping.
steps: For the smoothest hummus, pinch the skins off the chickpeas (or simmer them for 10 minutes with ½ tsp bicarb, then rinse).
Blend the tahini and lemon first until creamy.
Add the chickpeas, garlic and oil, and blend for 3–4 minutes, adding water until silky.
Serve with warm pitta.
tip: Removing the chickpea skins and blending for longer gives a much smoother result. Tahini is smooth ground sesame, not whole seeds.

storage.text: Keep in a sealed tub in the fridge for 3 days, or freeze for 2 months. Stir well after thawing.

title: Banana oat breakfast bars
summary: Soft, nut-free baked oat bars — grab one on the way out or pack for later.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mash the bananas, then beat in the eggs, milk and honey.
Blitz the oats briefly in a blender, then stir them in with the cinnamon and baking powder.
Spread into the tin and bake for 25 minutes until set and golden.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 8 bars.
tip: No nuts, seeds or dried fruit. Blitzing the oats gives a smoother bar.
swaps: Use maple syrup instead of honey
Use any milk, including oat milk

storage.text: Keep in a sealed tub in the fridge for 3 days, or wrap bars individually and freeze for 3 months. Thaw overnight or warm for 20 seconds in the microwave.

title: Peanut butter overnight oats
summary: Five-ingredient oats that soften overnight — make it the night before.
steps: Stir everything together in a jar or bowl.
Cover and chill overnight, or for at least 4 hours.
Stir and add a splash more milk if it's too thick. Eat cold or warm it through.
tip: Soaking makes oats very soft. Use smooth nut butter only.
swaps: Swap peanut butter for smooth almond butter or tahini
Use plant yoghurt and milk to make it vegan

storage.text: Make 2 jars at once — they keep for 2 days in the fridge. Don't freeze.

title: Mango & silken tofu smoothie
summary: Creamy, dairy-free and packed with protein from silken tofu.
steps: Put everything in a blender.
Blend for a full minute until completely smooth.
Drink straight away.
tip: Mango and banana have no seeds or tough skins once peeled. Silken tofu blends invisibly.
swaps: Use soya milk and maple syrup for a vegan version

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps in a sealed bottle in the fridge for 1 day — shake well.

title: Cinnamon French toast with apple
summary: Golden eggy bread with soft, buttery cinnamon apples.
steps: Cook the apples in a little butter with half the cinnamon for 8–10 minutes until very soft.
Whisk the eggs, milk and remaining cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Soak each slice of bread for a few seconds on each side.
Fry in butter over a medium heat for 2–3 minutes each side until golden.
Serve topped with the apples and honey.
tip: Peeling and cooking the apple removes the skin and softens the fibre.
swaps: Use pears instead of apples
Fry sliced banana in butter instead of apple

storage.text: Best fresh. Cooked French toast can be frozen for 1 month and reheated in a toaster. The apples keep 3 days in the fridge.

title: Cottage cheese pancakes
summary: Light, high-protein pancakes blended smooth with cottage cheese.
ingredients: Sliced banana or stewed pear, to serve
steps: Blend the cottage cheese and eggs until smooth.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and sugar.
Heat a little butter in a non-stick pan over a medium-low heat.
Cook small spoonfuls for 2 minutes each side until golden and set.
Serve with banana or stewed pear.
tip: Blending the cottage cheese gives a smooth batter and adds plenty of protein.
swaps: Use ricotta instead of cottage cheese

storage.text: Cool, then stack with baking paper between. Fridge for 2 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat in a toaster or dry pan.

title: Cheese & courgette egg muffins
summary: Baked mini omelettes — perfect for lunchboxes and busy mornings.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 6-hole muffin tin.
Squeeze the grated courgette dry in a clean tea towel.
Beat the eggs and milk, then stir in the courgette, cheese and chives.
Pour into the tin and bake for 18–20 minutes until set in the middle.
Cool for 5 minutes before lifting out.
tip: Peeled, grated and baked courgette is very soft. Squeezing out the water stops them going soggy.
swaps: Use wilted, finely chopped spinach instead of courgette
Use feta instead of cheddar

storage.text: Fridge in a sealed tub for 2 days, or freeze for 2 months. Reheat until piping hot, or eat cold from the fridge.

title: Cauliflower & cheddar soup
summary: Like cauliflower cheese in a bowl — velvety and comforting.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes.
Add the potato, cauliflower and stock. Simmer for 15–20 minutes until very soft.
Add the milk and blend until completely smooth.
Stir in the cheese and mustard over a low heat until melted.
tip: Cauliflower can cause wind for some people — start with a small bowl.
swaps: Use broccoli florets (no stalks) instead of half the cauliflower

storage.text: Freeze before adding the cheese for the best texture, then stir it in when reheating. Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months.

title: Silky spinach & potato soup
summary: A bright green soup that gets spinach in without any stringy leaves.
ingredients: Squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spinach for 2 minutes until wilted.
Blend until completely smooth, then add nutmeg and crème fraîche.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and season with salt to taste.
tip: Blending the spinach fully avoids the stringy texture. A squeeze of lemon adds brightness.
swaps: Use a splash of oat cream to make it dairy-free

storage.text: Cool quickly, then fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Add the crème fraîche after reheating.

title: Red pepper & butter bean soup
summary: Sweet, smoky and creamy, with blended butter beans for protein.
ingredients: 400g tin butter beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the peppers, butter beans and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend for 2–3 minutes until completely smooth.
Push through a fine sieve to remove any bean skins.
tip: Whole beans have tough skins, so blend this very well and sieve if you're unsure. Try a small portion first.
swaps: Use cannellini beans instead of butter beans

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Loosen with a little water when reheating.

title: Ginger egg drop soup
summary: A light, soothing broth with silky ribbons of egg — ready in minutes.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Simmer the stock, ginger and soy sauce for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornflour mix and simmer until slightly thickened.
Stir the soup in a circle and slowly pour in the eggs in a thin stream.
Add the tofu and leave for 30 seconds, then stir gently and serve.
tip: Very quick and soft — handy on harder days.
swaps: Add cubes of silken tofu for extra protein
Add a nest of soft udon noodles to make it more filling

storage.text: Best fresh. Leftovers keep 1 day in the fridge — reheat gently until steaming.

title: Cheese & chive potato cakes
summary: Crisp outside, fluffy inside — a great use for leftover mash.
ingredients: 2 tbsp plain flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Boil the potatoes until very soft. Drain well and mash smooth.
Mix in the cheese, egg yolk, chives and flour. Season.
With floured hands, shape into 8 cakes. Chill for 15 minutes if they feel soft.
Fry in a little oil and butter for 3–4 minutes each side until golden.
tip: Peeled, well-mashed potato is one of the gentlest starchy foods.
swaps: Use mashed sweet potato for half the potato

storage.text: Freeze uncooked cakes between baking paper for 3 months and fry from frozen (add a few minutes). Cooked cakes keep 2 days in the fridge.

title: Soft egg & onion rice bowl
summary: Japanese-style eggs gently set in a sweet soy broth over white rice.
steps: Simmer the onion in the stock, soy and honey for 8–10 minutes until very soft.
Pour the eggs over the onions. Cover and cook on a low heat for 2–3 minutes until just set.
Slide on to bowls of hot rice.
tip: Simmering the onion until very soft makes it much easier to digest.
swaps: Add cubes of firm tofu with the onion

storage.text: Best eaten straight away. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour and eat within 1 day.

title: Spanish potato tortilla
summary: A thick, soft potato omelette — good hot, cold or in a lunchbox.
steps: Cook the potatoes and onion gently in the oil in a 20cm non-stick pan for 20 minutes, until very soft but not browned.
Drain off most of the oil. Beat the eggs with salt and stir in the potatoes.
Return to the pan and cook on a low heat for 8–10 minutes until almost set.
Flip on to a plate and slide back in for 3–4 minutes — or skip the flip and finish under a hot grill for 3–4 minutes.
tip: Cooking the potato and onion slowly until soft keeps it gentle.
swaps: Leave out the onion if it doesn't suit you

storage.text: Cool, wrap and keep in the fridge for 2 days. Eat cold or warm gently. Don't freeze — the egg goes watery.

title: Red lentil bolognese
summary: A rich, family-friendly ragu that freezes brilliantly.
ingredients: 1 tbsp soy sauce or vegetarian Worcestershire sauce
Vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, to serve
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato purée for 2 minutes, then add the lentils, passata, soy sauce, stock and oregano.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the lentils have broken down.
Cook the spaghetti until soft and serve with the sauce and cheese.
tip: Grated carrot and red lentils melt into the sauce. Blend half for a smoother texture.
swaps: Use any pasta shape
Serve over mashed potato instead of pasta

storage.text: Freeze the sauce in portions for 3 months, or fridge for 3 days. Cook pasta fresh.

title: Mild tofu & spinach korma
summary: A creamy, gently spiced curry with no nuts and no chilli.
ingredients: 280g calcium-set firm tofu, pressed and cubed
steps: Fry the tofu in the oil until golden. Set aside.
Soften the onion for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk and spinach, simmer for 5 minutes, then blend smooth.
Stir in the tofu and honey. Take off the heat and stir in the yoghurt.
Serve with rice.
tip: Korma is usually thickened with nuts — this version uses blended onion and yoghurt instead.
swaps: Use paneer instead of tofu
Use coconut yoghurt to make it vegan

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Reheat gently — don't let it boil after the yoghurt goes in. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day; reheat only once.

title: Lentil & squash lasagne
summary: Layers of soft lentil ragu, squash and creamy white sauce — a freezer favourite.
ingredients: 1 batch red lentil bolognese sauce (sauce only, no spaghetti)
300g butternut squash, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Make a white sauce: melt the butter, stir in the flour, then slowly whisk in the milk until thick. Stir in half the cheese.
Layer the ragu, lasagne sheets, squash slices and white sauce in a large dish, three times, finishing with white sauce.
Top with the rest of the cheese.
Bake for 45 minutes until the pasta and squash are soft. Rest for 10 minutes.
tip: Thin squash slices bake until very tender. Check with a knife before serving.
swaps: Use courgette (peeled) instead of squash

storage.text: Freeze whole or in portions for 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight, then reheat covered until piping hot.

title: Cheesy leek & potato gratin
summary: Thin potato slices baked in garlicky cream with soft leeks and cheese.
ingredients: 2 leeks, white parts only, very finely chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Soften the leeks in the butter for 15 minutes until silky.
Warm the cream, milk and garlic with a pinch of salt and nutmeg. Layer the potatoes and leeks in a dish.
Pour over the cream and top with cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 50 minutes, then uncover for 20 minutes until golden and a knife slides through easily.
tip: Rich, so keep portions moderate if high-fat food bothers you.
swaps: Use half stock, half milk for a lighter version

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days or freeze in portions for 2 months. Reheat covered in the oven.

title: Saag paneer
summary: Paneer in a smooth, buttery spinach sauce — iron and protein together.
ingredients: White basmati rice or plain naan, to serve
Squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste
steps: Fry the paneer in half the butter until golden. Set aside.
Soften the onion in the rest of the butter for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the spinach in batches until wilted.
Blend the sauce until completely smooth.
Stir in the cream and paneer and heat through.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and season with salt to taste.
tip: Blending makes the spinach smooth. No chilli — warmth comes from ginger and cumin.
swaps: Use firm tofu instead of paneer

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. The paneer may firm up slightly after freezing. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day; reheat only once.

servedWith: White basmati rice or plain naan

title: Mild egg & tomato curry
summary: Soft-boiled eggs in a smooth, fragrant tomato and coconut sauce.
ingredients: Squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder.
Add the passata and coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend smooth.
Halve the eggs, add to the sauce and warm through. Serve with rice.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and season with salt to taste.
tip: Check your curry powder is labelled mild and has no chilli high on the list.
swaps: Add cubes of peeled sweet potato to bulk it out

storage.text: Freeze the sauce on its own for 3 months and add freshly boiled eggs. With eggs, keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day; reheat only once.

title: Courgette & ricotta pasta
summary: Five ingredients, twenty minutes — silky, lemony and very gentle.
ingredients: 1 lemon, zested, plus a squeeze of juice
steps: Cook the pasta until soft. Keep a cup of the water.
Cook the courgettes and garlic in the butter for 8 minutes until very soft.
Stir in the ricotta, hard cheese, lemon zest and a splash of pasta water to make a creamy sauce.
Toss with the pasta and season.
tip: Peeled, well-cooked courgette is one of the easiest vegetables to tolerate.
swaps: Add grated vegetarian hard cheese on top
Use cream cheese instead of ricotta

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; add a splash of water when reheating. Don't freeze.

title: Slow-cooker lentil & sweet potato stew
summary: Fifteen minutes of prep, then it cooks itself. Makes six freezer portions.
steps: Put everything except the lemon into a slow cooker.
Cook on low for 6–8 hours, or high for 4 hours, until everything is very soft.
Mash or blend some of it for a thicker, smoother stew.
Add lemon and season before serving.
tip: The time shown is 15 minutes' prep plus 4 hours on high; on low allow 6–8 hours.
swaps: No slow cooker? Simmer in a covered pan for 40 minutes, stirring often.

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Loosen with water when reheating.

title: Creamy baked feta pasta
summary: A block of feta baked in passata, then stirred into a creamy sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Pour the passata into a baking dish, stir in the garlic and oil, and put the feta in the middle.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta until soft.
Mash the feta into the sauce, then stir in the pasta and basil.
tip: The viral version uses cherry tomatoes, which have skins and seeds. Passata gives the same flavour without them.
swaps: Stir in wilted, finely chopped spinach

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water. The sauce alone freezes for 2 months.

title: Spinach & feta filo pie
summary: Golden filo layers over a soft, cheesy spinach and egg filling.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Wilt the spinach, squeeze out the water and chop very finely.
Mix with the feta, ricotta, eggs, nutmeg and dill.
Line a 20cm square dish with 3 buttered filo sheets, add the filling and lay 3 more buttered sheets flat on top.
Cover with foil for the first 20 minutes for a softer top, then bake uncovered for 10–15 minutes until golden and set.
tip: Leave off the sesame seeds often scattered on top. Chew the crisp filo well.
swaps: Use cheddar instead of feta for a milder flavour

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days, or freeze (baked) for 2 months. Reheat in the oven so the pastry crisps up.

title: Silky chocolate pots
summary: Three ingredients — rich chocolate mousse made with silken tofu. Needs 1 hour to chill.
steps: Blend the tofu until completely smooth.
Add the melted chocolate and maple syrup and blend again.
Spoon into small pots and chill for at least 1 hour.
tip: A smooth, protein-rich pudding. Dark chocolate has some caffeine, so go easy if that affects you.
swaps: Use milk chocolate for a milder flavour

storage.text: Cover and keep in the fridge for 3 days. Don't freeze.

title: Banana & peanut butter ice cream
summary: Two-ingredient soft-serve made from frozen banana.
steps: Let the frozen banana sit for 5 minutes.
Blend with the peanut butter, scraping down the sides, until smooth and creamy.
Eat straight away as soft-serve, or freeze for 1 hour for a firmer scoop.
tip: Freeze ripe bananas in slices so they're always ready.
swaps: Leave out the peanut butter, or swap for 1 tbsp cocoa powder

storage.text: Best eaten fresh. Freeze leftovers in a tub for up to 1 month — let it soften for 10 minutes before scooping.

title: Baked egg custard
summary: A classic, wobbly vanilla custard with nutmeg — soft, simple and nourishing.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan).
Warm the milk until steaming. Whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla, then whisk in the milk.
Strain into an ovenproof dish and grate over nutmeg.
Stand the dish in a roasting tin half-filled with hot water.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
tip: Gentle protein and calcium for days when eating feels hard.
swaps: Add a strip of lemon zest to the milk while it warms

storage.text: Cool, cover and keep in the fridge for 2 days. Eat cold. Don't freeze.

title: Semolina pudding with jam
summary: Creamy, comforting semolina with a swirl of seedless jam.
steps: Warm the milk in a pan.
Whisk in the semolina and sugar.
Simmer, stirring constantly, for 8–10 minutes until thick and smooth.
Stir in the vanilla and serve with a spoonful of jam.
tip: Choose seedless jam (such as apricot or seedless raspberry) to avoid tiny seeds.
swaps: Use stewed pear or apple instead of jam

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Reheat with a splash of milk. Don't freeze.

title: Apple & cinnamon muffins
summary: Soft, nut-free muffins with peeled, grated apple.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, cinnamon, bicarb and sugar.
Beat the eggs, milk and butter, then stir into the dry mix with the apple until just combined.
Divide between the cases and bake for 20 minutes until risen and golden.
tip: Grated, peeled apple bakes right into the crumb — no chunks or skin.
swaps: Use peeled pear instead of apple

storage.text: Keep in a tin at room temperature for 3 days, or freeze for 3 months. Thaw at room temperature or warm for 15 seconds.

title: Cheese scones
summary: Fluffy, savoury scones — great with soup or in a lunchbox.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a baking tray.
Rub the butter into the flour and baking powder until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in most of the cheese and the mustard, then the milk, to make a soft dough.
Pat out to 2.5cm thick, cut into 8 rounds and brush with milk. Top with the rest of the cheese.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until risen and golden.
tip: White flour scones are lower in fibre than wholemeal ones.
swaps: Add 1 tbsp snipped chives to the dough

storage.text: Best on the day. Keep in a tin at room temperature for 2 days, or freeze for 3 months and warm through in the oven.

title: Mango lassi
summary: A cool, creamy yoghurt drink with sweet mango.
steps: Blend everything until completely smooth.
Taste and add more honey if needed. Serve chilled.
tip: A creamy, calcium-rich snack.
swaps: Use soya yoghurt and milk to make it dairy-free

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps 1 day in a sealed bottle in the fridge — shake before drinking.

title: Nourishing banana milkshake
summary: An energy- and protein-rich shake for days when eating a full meal feels hard.
steps: Put everything in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth and frothy.
Drink straight away, slowly.
tip: Milk powder adds protein and energy without extra volume. Sip it over 20–30 minutes if a full glass feels like a lot.
swaps: Use 2 tbsp Greek yoghurt instead of milk powder
Leave out the peanut butter for a lighter shake

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps 1 day in a sealed bottle in the fridge — shake well.

title: Silky steamed egg custard
summary: A Japanese-style savoury custard (chawanmushi) — wobbly, gentle and high in protein.
ingredients: 1 tsp mirin or a pinch of sugar
steps: Whisk the eggs gently, without making them foamy.
Stir in the stock, soy, ginger and mirin, then strain through a sieve into 2 heatproof bowls or mugs.
Cover each with foil.
Steam over gently simmering water for 12–15 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
tip: Straining gives a perfectly smooth texture. Keep the water at a gentle simmer so it stays silky, not spongy.
swaps: Add a few cubes of silken tofu before steaming

storage.text: Best eaten warm and fresh. Can be kept covered in the fridge for 1 day and eaten cold. Don't freeze.

title: Lemon & egg orzo soup
summary: Greek avgolemono — a velvety, bright soup thickened with egg and lemon.
steps: Bring the stock to the boil and cook the orzo for 10 minutes until soft.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice in a bowl.
Slowly whisk 2 ladles of hot stock into the eggs.
Take the pan off the heat and stir the egg mix in. Stir for 1 minute until silky — don't let it boil.
Season and serve.
tip: Adding hot stock to the eggs first stops them scrambling.
swaps: Use white rice instead of orzo
Stir in finely chopped dill at the end

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently without boiling, or the egg will split. Don't freeze.

title: Ginger rice congee
summary: Slow-cooked rice porridge with ginger and soy, topped with a soft egg.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized piece (3cm) fresh ginger, peeled and sliced
steps: Put the rice, stock and ginger in a large pan and bring to the boil.
Simmer very gently, partly covered, for 45–50 minutes, stirring now and then, until creamy and broken down.
Remove the ginger slices and stir in the soy.
Meanwhile, boil the eggs for 6½ minutes, cool and peel.
Serve the congee topped with a halved egg and a few drops of sesame oil.
tip: Congee is one of the gentlest foods there is — the rice breaks down completely. Sesame oil has no seeds.
swaps: Add cubes of silken tofu instead of egg

storage.text: Contains rice: cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Reheat once with a splash of water until steaming. Don't freeze.

title: Vegetarian kedgeree
summary: Buttery, mildly spiced rice with soft-boiled eggs and lemon.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 8 minutes. Stir in the spices for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stock, cover and simmer for 12 minutes until the rice is tender.
Meanwhile, boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool and peel.
Fluff the rice with lemon juice and parsley, then top with the quartered eggs.
tip: Traditional kedgeree uses smoked fish — eggs carry it here. Check the curry powder is mild.
swaps: Add flakes of smoked tofu
Stir in a spoonful of crème fraîche for creaminess

storage.text: Contains rice: cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Reheat once until steaming hot. Don't freeze.

title: Poached eggs on herby yoghurt
summary: Turkish çılbır — soft poached eggs on creamy yoghurt with warm paprika butter.
steps: Let the yoghurt come to room temperature and stir in the garlic and a pinch of salt. Spread on 2 plates.
Poach the eggs in gently simmering water for 3 minutes.
Melt the butter with the paprika until it foams.
Put the eggs on the yoghurt, spoon over the paprika butter and scatter with dill. Serve with bread.
tip: Sweet paprika gives the colour without the chilli flakes used in the original.
swaps: Leave out the garlic if raw garlic doesn't suit you

storage.text: Best eaten straight away.

title: Ricotta gnudi with sage butter
summary: Pillowy ricotta dumplings in nutty sage butter — like the filling of ravioli, without the pasta.
ingredients: 60g plain flour, plus extra for rolling
steps: Mix the ricotta, egg, cheese, nutmeg and flour into a soft dough.
With floured hands, roll into walnut-sized balls and dust with flour. Chill for 20 minutes.
Cook in gently simmering salted water for 3–4 minutes until they float.
Meanwhile, melt the butter with the sage until it smells nutty.
Toss the gnudi in the sage butter and serve with extra cheese.
tip: Very soft and rich in protein and calcium. Lift the sage leaves out before serving if you'd rather not chew them.
swaps: Serve in smooth tomato sauce instead of sage butter

storage.text: Freeze uncooked gnudi on a tray, then bag for 2 months — cook from frozen for 5–6 minutes. Cooked gnudi keep 2 days in the fridge.

title: Silky beetroot soup
summary: A deep pink, sweet and earthy blended borscht with dill soured cream.
ingredients: 1 tbsp red wine vinegar or lemon juice
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the beetroot, potato and stock. Simmer for 30 minutes until very soft.
Blend until completely smooth and stir in the vinegar. Season.
Serve with a spoonful of soured cream mixed with the dill.
tip: Peeled and blended beetroot is soft and smooth. It can turn your wee and poo pink or red — that's harmless and expected.
swaps: Use ready-cooked beetroot (not in vinegar) and simmer for 15 minutes

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Add the soured cream after reheating.

title: Lemon posset
summary: Three ingredients — a silky, sharp-sweet set cream pudding. Needs 3 hours to set.
steps: Heat the cream and sugar, stirring, until it just comes to the boil. Bubble for 2 minutes.
Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice and zest.
Strain into 4 small glasses and chill for at least 3 hours until set.
tip: Rich, so the portions are small. Straining removes the zest for a perfectly smooth finish.
swaps: Use oranges for a milder flavour

storage.text: Cover and keep in the fridge for 3 days. Don't freeze.

title: Butternut & silken tofu soup
summary: Silky squash soup with silken tofu blended in for protein you can't taste.
ingredients: 600g butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and cubed
Squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the squash and stock and simmer for 20 minutes until very soft.
Add the tofu and nutmeg and blend until completely smooth.
Finish with lemon and salt.
tip: Silken tofu adds protein to a gentle soup without changing the texture.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato instead of squash

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Blend again after thawing if it separates.

title: Cheesy egg-enriched mash
summary: Extra-smooth mash with egg yolk and cheese beaten in — soft, filling and nourishing.
ingredients: 500g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until very soft. Drain well.
Mash until completely smooth, or push through a sieve.
Over a low heat, beat in the butter, milk, egg yolks and cheese for 2 minutes until glossy and hot.
Season and serve.
tip: Beating the yolks into hot mash cooks them through and adds protein and energy when appetite is low.
swaps: Use oat milk and olive oil for a dairy-free version, and leave out the cheese

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Freezes for 1 month but may go a little grainy — beat in a splash of milk when reheating until piping hot.

title: Vanilla protein shake
summary: A creamy, energy-rich shake made from everyday ingredients — no protein powder needed.
steps: Blend everything until smooth and frothy.
Drink chilled, slowly.
tip: Milk powder roughly doubles the protein of a glass of milk without making it bigger.
swaps: Add ½ ripe banana for a thicker shake

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps 1 day in a sealed bottle in the fridge — shake well.

title: Smooth herby cottage cheese dip
summary: A no-cook, high-protein dip blended until silky, with soft warm pitta.
ingredients: 1 tbsp very finely chopped dill or chives
1 lemon, zested, plus a squeeze of juice
steps: Blend the cottage cheese and oil until completely smooth.
Stir in the herbs, lemon zest and juice. Season.
Serve with warm pitta, cut into strips.
tip: Blending removes the curds for a smooth texture. Leave out the herbs on harder days.
swaps: Use ricotta instead of cottage cheese

storage.text: Keep covered in the fridge for 3 days. Don't freeze.

title: Yoghurt & seedless jam pot
summary: A no-cook snack in two minutes — thick yoghurt swirled with smooth jam.
steps: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl or jar.
Swirl through the jam and honey.
tip: Check the jam says seedless — raspberry and strawberry jams usually have seeds.
swaps: Use stewed pear or apple instead of jam

storage.text: Best made fresh. Can be made the night before and kept covered in the fridge.

title: Peanut butter & banana toast
summary: A quick, filling snack — smooth peanut butter and mashed banana on soft white toast.
steps: Toast the bread lightly.
Spread with peanut butter.
Mash the banana on top and sprinkle with cinnamon.
tip: Lightly toasted white bread is softer than very crisp toast. Use smooth nut butter only.
swaps: Use smooth tahini instead of peanut butter

storage.text: Best eaten straight away.

title: Poached eggs on buttery mash
summary: A light, gentle supper — soft poached eggs on smooth mash with a little chive butter.
ingredients: 500g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until very soft. Drain and mash smooth with the butter and milk.
Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer and poach the eggs for 3 minutes.
Spoon the mash on to plates, top with the eggs and scatter over the chives.
tip: Lower in fat than most comfort food, and soft all the way through.
swaps: Use mashed sweet potato instead

storage.text: Best eaten straight away. Leftover mash keeps 2 days in the fridge — cook eggs fresh.

title: Soft couscous with roast squash
summary: Fluffy lemon couscous with tender roast squash and crumbled feta. Light and quick.
ingredients: 300g butternut squash, peeled and cut into small cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the squash with the oil and cumin and roast for 25 minutes until very soft.
Pour the hot stock over the couscous, cover and leave for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon zest and juice.
Top with the squash, feta and parsley.
tip: Couscous is made from refined wheat and is soft and quick. Use the finest you can find.
swaps: Use paneer or halloumi instead of feta
Use white rice instead of couscous

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Eat cold or reheat until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Potato & cheese pierogi
summary: Polish dumplings filled with cheesy mash, served with soft buttery onions and soured cream.
ingredients: 300g plain flour, plus extra for rolling
steps: Mix the flour, egg, water and oil into a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes until very soft, then mash smooth with the cottage cheese and cheddar. Season and cool.
Cook the onions in the butter over a low heat for 25 minutes until very soft and golden.
Roll the dough thinly, cut 8cm circles, add a spoonful of filling and pinch the edges closed.
Cook in simmering salted water for 3–4 minutes after they float.
Toss in the onions and butter, and serve with soured cream.
tip: Cook the onions low and slow until they're very soft. Chew the dumpling edges well.
swaps: Leave out the onions and use melted butter with a little dill

storage.text: Freeze uncooked pierogi on a tray, then bag for 3 months — boil from frozen for 6–7 minutes. Cooked pierogi keep 2 days in the fridge.

title: Pumpkin & tofu coconut curry
summary: A fragrant Thai-style curry without curry paste or chilli — lemongrass, lime and ginger do the work.
ingredients: 500g pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled and cubed
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the ginger for 1 minute.
Add the lemongrass, pumpkin, coconut milk, stock, soy and sugar. Simmer for 15–20 minutes until the pumpkin is very soft.
Remove the lemongrass. Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice and serve with rice.
tip: Lemongrass is too fibrous to eat, so it's always removed before serving. Most Thai curry pastes contain chilli and shrimp, so this doesn't use one.
swaps: Use paneer instead of tofu
Use light coconut milk for a lighter curry

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day; reheat only once.

title: Japanese rolled omelette (tamagoyaki)
summary: Lightly sweet, soft layers of egg rolled up in a small pan and sliced into tender pieces.
ingredients: 1 tsp neutral oil, such as vegetable oil
steps: Whisk the eggs, sugar, soy sauce and milk together well, without making it too frothy.
Heat a small non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat and wipe it with a little oil on kitchen paper.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and tilt to cover the pan. When it is just set but still slightly wet on top, roll it up from the far side towards you with a spatula.
Push the roll to the far side, wipe the pan with a little more oil and pour in another thin layer, lifting the roll so the egg runs underneath. When just set, roll it back towards you.
Repeat until all the egg is used. Tip onto a board, wrap in a clean tea towel for 2 minutes to firm up, then slice into thick pieces.
tip: Cooking over a low heat keeps the layers soft and pale rather than browned and crisp. It uses only a teaspoon of oil, so it stays light.
swaps: Leave out the sugar and add a pinch of salt for a savoury version
Use 1 tbsp vegetable stock instead of milk for a more traditional flavour

storage.text: Lovely cold in a lunchbox. Cool quickly, cover and keep in the fridge for up to 1 day. Don't freeze.

title: Mild egg bhurji on toast
summary: Indian-style soft scrambled eggs with gently cooked onion, a little passata and warm, mild spices.
ingredients: 4 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
1 tbsp fresh coriander, very finely chopped (optional)
2 slices white bread, toasted and buttered
steps: Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat and cook the onion gently for 8–10 minutes until very soft and sweet, not browned.
Stir in the cumin and turmeric for 30 seconds, then add the passata and simmer for 2 minutes.
Pour in the eggs and stir slowly over a low heat until softly set and creamy.
Stir through the coriander, if using, and spoon onto the buttered toast.
tip: Bhurji is usually made with green chilli and raw tomato; here passata and well-cooked onion give the same comforting flavour with no heat or skins.
swaps: Serve with a soft white chapati or roti instead of toast
Stir in a handful of very finely chopped baby spinach with the passata

storage.text: Best eaten straight away. Any leftover egg should be cooled quickly, kept covered in the fridge and eaten within 1 day, reheated once until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Soft carrot upma
summary: A South Indian savoury semolina porridge with soft grated carrot, ginger and a squeeze of lemon.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp fresh ginger, finely grated (discard any stringy fibres)
steps: Toast the semolina in a dry pan over a medium heat, stirring, for 3–4 minutes until it smells toasty. Tip into a bowl.
Melt the butter or ghee in the same pan and cook the onion and carrot gently for 8 minutes until very soft.
Stir in the ginger and turmeric for 30 seconds, then pour in the hot water and salt and bring to the boil.
Turn the heat to low and pour in the semolina in a slow stream, stirring constantly so no lumps form.
Cover and cook for 3 minutes until thick and soft, then stir in the lemon juice and serve.
tip: Traditional upma often includes mustard seeds, curry leaves, nuts and green chilli; they are left out here to keep it soft and mild. Grating the carrot finely means it cooks right down.
swaps: Use a peeled, finely grated courgette instead of the carrot
Serve with a spoonful of plain yoghurt on top

storage.text: Cool, cover and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. It firms up as it cools: loosen with a splash of hot water and reheat until piping hot.

title: Ground rice porridge with peach purée
summary: A silky, vanilla-scented milk porridge made with ground rice and swirled with soft peach purée.
ingredients: 2 ripe peaches, peeled, stoned and chopped
steps: Whisk the ground rice and sugar into the cold milk in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, then cook for 5–6 minutes until thick and smooth. Stir in the vanilla.
Meanwhile, simmer the peaches with the water and cinnamon in a small covered pan for 8–10 minutes until very soft, then mash or blend until smooth.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and swirl the peach purée through.
tip: To peel peaches easily, cut a small cross in the base, cover with boiling water for 1 minute, then slip the peel off. Ground rice gives a completely smooth porridge with no chewing needed.
swaps: Use a 410g tin of peach slices in juice, drained and blended, instead of fresh peaches
Use semolina instead of ground rice

storage.text: Best made fresh. If keeping leftovers, cool within 1 hour, keep covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day, reheating once until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Baked vanilla oats with pear
summary: A soft, custardy tray of baked porridge with soft grated pear, ready to slice for the week.
ingredients: 25g butter, melted, plus a little for greasing
2 very ripe pears, peeled, cored and coarsely grated
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and grease a 20cm square baking dish with a little butter.
Mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, maple syrup, vanilla and melted butter together, then stir into the oats with the grated pear.
Pour into the dish and bake for 30–35 minutes until just set and lightly golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares and serve warm.
tip: Baking the oats in milk makes them very soft, and grated ripe pear melts into the mix with no firm pieces. Choose plain porridge oats rather than jumbo oats for the softest result.
swaps: Use 2 mashed ripe bananas instead of the pears and leave out the maple syrup
Use 1 peeled, finely grated eating apple instead of the pears

storage.text: Cool, cut into portions and keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days, or wrap individually and freeze for up to 2 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat with a splash of milk until piping hot.

title: Homemade crumpets
summary: Soft, bubbly British crumpets made from a simple yeasted batter that freeze well.
steps: Mix both flours, the sugar and yeast in a large bowl. Whisk in the warm milk to make a thick, smooth batter and beat for 3 minutes.
Cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1 hour until bubbly and nearly doubled.
Stir the bicarbonate of soda and salt into the warm water, beat it into the batter, then leave for 20 minutes.
Heat a heavy frying pan over a low-medium heat. Grease the pan and four 9cm crumpet or egg rings well with oil.
Sit the rings in the pan and spoon in batter to about 1cm deep. Cook for 8–10 minutes until the tops are covered in holes and just set.
Lift off the rings, flip the crumpets and cook for 1 minute more. Repeat with the rest of the batter, re-greasing the rings each time.
Toast and spread with butter to serve.
tip: Made with white flour only, these are soft and plain. Keep the heat low so the bases cook through without burning.
swaps: Use all plain flour if you have no bread flour (slightly less chewy)
Top with smooth peanut butter or seedless jam instead of butter

storage.text: Makes about 12. Cool on a rack, then keep in an airtight tin for up to 2 days, or freeze in a bag for up to 3 months and toast straight from frozen.

title: Swedish cardamom pancakes
summary: Thin, tender Swedish-style pancakes with a hint of cardamom, folded and served with smooth jam.
ingredients: 25g butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
steps: Whisk the flour, cardamom, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add the eggs and half the milk and whisk to a smooth, thick batter.
Whisk in the rest of the milk and the melted butter, then leave to rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and add a little butter. Pour in a small ladle of batter and swirl to coat the pan thinly.
Cook for about 1 minute until set, flip and cook for 30 seconds more. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Fold into quarters and serve with the seedless jam.
tip: In Sweden these come with lingonberry jam, which contains seeds — use a smooth seedless jam instead.
swaps: Fill with a spoonful of stewed peeled apple instead of jam
Use ground cinnamon instead of cardamom

storage.text: Makes about 12. Cool, stack between sheets of baking paper and keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Warm in a dry pan or the microwave until hot.

title: Batch-and-freeze drop scones
summary: Small, fluffy Scotch pancakes that freeze well for quick breakfasts warmed in the toaster.
ingredients: 15g butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and sugar in a bowl and make a well in the middle.
Add the egg and half the milk and whisk to a smooth paste, then whisk in the rest of the milk and the melted butter to make a thick, pourable batter.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and wipe with a little butter.
Drop in tablespoons of batter, spaced apart. Cook for 1–2 minutes until bubbles appear on top, then flip and cook for 1 minute more.
Keep warm wrapped in a clean tea towel while you cook the rest.
tip: Plain white flour and a soft, fluffy texture make these an easy breakfast. Wrapping them in a tea towel as they cook keeps them soft rather than crisp.
swaps: Fold 1 mashed ripe banana into the batter
Serve with a spoonful of thick yoghurt and smooth peach purée

storage.text: Makes about 16. Cool under a tea towel, then keep in an airtight tin for 1 day, or freeze between sheets of baking paper for up to 3 months. Warm from frozen in the toaster or microwave.

title: Soft-boiled eggs with buttered soldiers
summary: The classic 10-minute British breakfast: jammy eggs with strips of buttered white toast for dipping.
steps: Bring a small pan of water to the boil, gently lower in the eggs and simmer for 6 minutes for jammy yolks (5 minutes for runny).
Meanwhile, toast the bread, spread with the butter and cut into strips.
Sit the eggs in egg cups, slice off the tops, sprinkle with salt and dip in the soldiers.
tip: British Lion-stamped eggs are fine to eat soft-boiled. If you'd rather have a firmer yolk, simmer for 8 minutes.
swaps: Use soft brioche or a lightly toasted crumpet for dipping
Mash the eggs into a cup with a little butter for an even softer breakfast

storage.text: Eat straight away; soft-boiled eggs shouldn't be kept.

title: Lemony whipped butter beans on toast
summary: Butter beans warmed with garlic and cumin, then blended with lemon and yoghurt into a silky spread for toast.
ingredients: 400g tin butter beans, drained and rinsed
2 slices white sourdough or white bread
1 tbsp fresh parsley, very finely chopped (optional)
steps: Warm the oil in a small pan over a low heat and cook the garlic for 1 minute without browning.
Add the butter beans, water and cumin and simmer for 5 minutes until very soft.
Blend with the lemon juice and yoghurt until completely smooth (push through a sieve for extra silkiness), then season with salt and pepper.
Toast the bread, spread the warm bean purée thickly on top and scatter with parsley, if using.
tip: Blending the beans until completely smooth breaks down their skins. Use a mini food processor or stick blender rather than a fork for the smoothest result.
swaps: Use a 400g tin of chickpeas, simmered for 10 minutes and blended very smooth
Top with a soft poached egg for extra protein

storage.text: Keep the bean purée in a covered tub in the fridge for up to 3 days and spread on freshly made toast. Don't freeze (it contains yoghurt).

title: Mild breakfast quesadillas
summary: Soft scrambled egg and melted cheddar folded into toasted flour tortillas with a little smoky-sweet passata.
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk. Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat and stir the eggs until just softly set. Tip onto a plate and wipe the pan.
Mix the passata with the paprika.
Lay a tortilla in the dry pan, spread half of it with half the passata, scatter over a quarter of the cheese, then half the egg and another quarter of the cheese.
Fold the tortilla over and cook over a medium heat for 2 minutes each side until golden and the cheese has melted. Repeat with the second tortilla.
Cut into wedges and serve.
tip: There's no salsa, beans or jalapeño here — sweet paprika gives a gentle smoky flavour without heat. Pick tortillas with a short ingredient list.
swaps: Spread with a little mashed ripe avocado instead of passata
Use mozzarella instead of cheddar for a milder, stretchier filling

storage.text: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers can be cooled quickly, kept covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and reheated in a dry pan until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Ricotta & honey brioche with warm banana
summary: Soft toasted brioche spread with creamy ricotta, topped with buttery cinnamon banana and a drizzle of honey.
steps: Melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium heat, add the banana slices and cinnamon and cook for 1–2 minutes each side until soft and golden.
Lightly toast the brioche.
Spread the ricotta thickly over the brioche, pile the warm banana on top and drizzle with the honey.
tip: A small, energy-dense breakfast for low-appetite mornings. Toast the brioche only lightly so it stays soft.
swaps: Use soft cream cheese instead of ricotta
Use a soft, ripe peeled pear, sliced, instead of banana

storage.text: Best made fresh. Opened ricotta keeps covered in the fridge for 2–3 days; check the pack.

title: Soft tofu & spinach scramble
summary: Finely crumbled tofu cooked until creamy with golden turmeric, soy and a little wilted spinach, served on toast.
steps: Pat the tofu dry and crumble it very finely with a fork.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over a medium-low heat, add the turmeric and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the tofu and soy sauce and cook, stirring, for 3–4 minutes.
Add the spinach and milk and cook for 2 minutes more until the spinach has wilted and the mixture is creamy.
Spoon onto the toast and serve.
tip: Chopping the spinach very finely means it wilts right down to soft flecks. Check the tofu pack says calcium sulphate for extra calcium.
swaps: Use 3 tbsp passata instead of the spinach
Use soya milk instead of milk

storage.text: Keep leftovers in a covered tub in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat until piping hot, with a splash of milk to loosen. Don't freeze.

title: Silky roast carrot & tahini dip
summary: Sweet, soft-roasted carrots blended with a little tahini, lemon and yoghurt into a velvety dip.
ingredients: 4 soft white pittas, warmed, to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the carrots with the oil and cumin in a roasting tin.
Cover with foil and roast for 20 minutes, then uncover and roast for 15–20 minutes more until very soft.
Cool slightly, then blend with the tahini, lemon juice, yoghurt and water until completely smooth. Season with salt.
Serve with warm pitta, torn into strips.
tip: Covering the carrots for the first part of roasting keeps them soft rather than crisp at the edges. On a flare day, enjoy the dip on its own by the spoonful or with soft white bread.
swaps: Use peeled butternut squash instead of carrot
Use smooth cashew butter instead of tahini

storage.text: Keep in a covered tub in the fridge for up to 3 days. If you want to freeze it, blend without the yoghurt, freeze for up to 3 months, then stir the yoghurt in once defrosted.

title: Whipped feta & honey dip
summary: A no-cook, creamy whipped feta and yoghurt dip with lemon and a drizzle of honey.
ingredients: 4 soft white pittas, warmed and cut into strips, to serve
steps: Blitz the feta and yoghurt in a food processor for 2–3 minutes until completely smooth and fluffy.
Add the lemon juice and olive oil and blitz again briefly.
Spread onto a plate, drizzle with the honey and serve with the pitta strips.
tip: Feta is salty and quite rich, so this is one for good days. Blitzing for a few minutes gives a properly smooth, whipped texture with no crumbly bits.
swaps: Use half ricotta and half feta for a milder, less salty dip
Serve with very soft cooked, peeled carrot batons instead of pitta

storage.text: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; add the honey just before serving. Don't freeze.

title: No-cook beetroot & yoghurt dip
summary: A bright pink, mildly spiced dip made in minutes from ready-cooked beetroot and creamy yoghurt.
ingredients: 250g cooked beetroot (vacuum-packed, not in vinegar), chopped
1 tsp fresh dill, very finely chopped (optional)
4 soft white pittas or slices of white bread, to serve
steps: Blitz the beetroot in a food processor until completely smooth.
Add the yoghurt, cumin, lemon juice and a pinch of salt and blitz again until evenly pink and creamy.
Stir in the dill, if using, and serve with soft bread or pitta.
tip: Vacuum-packed cooked beetroot is already peeled and very soft, so there's no cooking needed. Beetroot can turn urine and stools pink or red for a day or two, which is harmless but worth knowing.
swaps: Use plain yoghurt for a lighter, looser dip
Use 1/2 tsp ground coriander instead of cumin

storage.text: Keep in a covered tub in the fridge for up to 3 days. Don't freeze (it contains yoghurt).

title: Soft cheddar breadsticks
summary: Soft, pull-apart white bread sticks baked with a little mature cheddar — a mild lunchbox snack that keeps well in a tin.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and a third of the cheese in a large bowl.
Add the warm milk and melted butter and mix to a soft dough (add a splash more milk if dry). Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and springy.
Cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1 hour until doubled in size.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a 20cm stick. Lay on the trays, cover loosely with a tea towel and leave for 15 minutes.
Brush with the beaten egg and scatter with the rest of the cheese and the paprika, if using.
Bake for 12–14 minutes until pale golden but still soft. Wrap in a clean tea towel as they cool so they stay soft.
tip: Unlike crisp pastry cheese straws, these stay soft and bready, with no hard shards. Take them out while still pale so the outsides stay tender.
swaps: Use vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese instead of cheddar
Use 1 tsp dried oregano instead of paprika

storage.text: Makes 12. Keep in an airtight tin for up to 2 days, or freeze in a bag for up to 3 months. Defrost at room temperature and warm briefly in the oven.

title: No-bake peanut butter oat bites
summary: Soft, fudgy no-bake bites of oats blitzed to a fine flour, smooth peanut butter and honey for lunchboxes and quick energy.
steps: Blitz the oats in a food processor for 1–2 minutes until they are a fine flour with no flakes left.

If the peanut butter is stiff, warm it with the honey in the microwave for 20 seconds. Mix the oats, peanut butter, honey, vanilla and salt into a soft dough, then leave for 10 minutes so the oats soften.
Roll into 14 small balls, about 1 tablespoon each, and roll in the grated chocolate, if using.
Put in the fridge for 30 minutes to firm up.
tip: Blitzing the oats to a fine flour gives a smooth, fudgy texture with no rough bits. Choose a peanut butter that is just peanuts and a little salt, and make sure it says smooth.
swaps: Use smooth almond butter or tahini instead of peanut butter
Use maple syrup instead of honey

storage.text: Keep in a covered tub in the fridge for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months and defrost in the fridge or a lunchbox for an hour.

title: Banana custard pots
summary: Homemade vanilla custard stirred with smooth mashed banana, served warm or cold in little pots.
steps: Heat the milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Whisk the egg yolks, sugar and cornflour together in a bowl, then slowly pour in the hot milk, whisking all the time.
Pour back into the pan and stir constantly over a low heat for 4–5 minutes until thick and smooth. Stir in the vanilla.
Mash the bananas until completely smooth (or blend them) and stir into the custard.
Spoon into 4 small pots and eat warm, or cool and keep in the fridge.
tip: The cornflour helps stop the custard from splitting, so it stays silky. Mashing the banana rather than slicing it keeps every spoonful smooth.
swaps: Use blended tinned peaches instead of banana
Use a good shop-bought fresh custard with a short ingredient list if you're too tired to make it

storage.text: Cover the surface with baking paper to stop a skin forming, then cool and keep in the fridge for up to 1 day (the banana darkens after that). Don't freeze.

title: Peach & vanilla yoghurt smoothie
summary: A no-cook, silky smoothie of tinned peaches, yoghurt, milk and vanilla.
ingredients: 410g tin peach slices in juice, drained
steps: Put the peaches, yoghurt, milk, vanilla and honey, if using, in a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth, then pour into glasses.
tip: Tinned peaches are already peeled and very soft, so they blend perfectly smooth. Choose ones in juice rather than syrup.
swaps: Use kefir instead of yoghurt
Use a very ripe peeled mango instead of peaches

storage.text: Best drunk straight away. Keep in a sealed bottle in the fridge for up to 1 day and shake well before drinking.

title: Warm golden milk
summary: A comforting mug of warm milk gently spiced with turmeric, ginger and cinnamon and sweetened with honey.
steps: Whisk the turmeric, ginger and cinnamon into the cold milk in a small pan.
Heat gently, whisking, until steaming but not boiling.
Stir in the honey and vanilla and pour into a mug.
tip: Whisking the ground spices into cold milk first stops them clumping. It's warming without any heat from chilli or pepper.
swaps: Use oat milk or soya milk instead of dairy milk
Use maple syrup instead of honey

storage.text: Best made fresh. Mix a larger batch of the dry spices and keep in a jar for quick mugs.

title: Cheese & passata pitta pizzas
summary: Quick mini pizzas on soft white pitta with smooth tomato sauce and melted mozzarella — good hot or cold.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Mix the passata, tomato purée and oregano and spread over the pittas.
Scatter over the mozzarella and drizzle with the oil.
Bake on a tray for 8–10 minutes until bubbling, then cool slightly and cut into strips.
